title: CRM's Cash Flow Strength: Can It Sustain Big Shareholder Returns?

CRM's Cash Flow Strength: Can It Sustain Big Shareholder Returns?

MSFT
ORCL

Trading disclosure

Salesforce, Inc. CRM is demonstrating strong cash-generating ability, giving it financial flexibility to return more capital to shareholders. Its growing free cash flow, ongoing share repurchases and dividend payments provide a solid foundation for investor returns.

In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Salesforce's operating cash flow jumped 71.5% year over year to $1.27 billion, while free cash flow increased 81.5% to $1.10 billion. In the first half of fiscal 2027, the company generated operating and free cash flows of $7.97 billion and $7.65 billion, respectively. This improvement highlights the strength of its subscription-based business, which provides recurring revenues and supports consistent cash generation.

Salesforce is putting this cash to work. The company paid $364 million in dividends during the quarter and continued its $25 billion accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program. This $25 billion ASR transaction represents the first half of a larger $50 billion share repurchase program authorized by the company's board of directors in February 2026.

Management expects the buyback to reduce outstanding shares by at least 14%. This could provide a meaningful boost to earnings per share while increasing the ownership stake of remaining shareholders. Through the first half of fiscal 2027, Salesforce's capital returns totaled $27.9 billion. The share count was down 141 million shares, or 15%, year over year.

Nevertheless, investors should be cautious about assuming that such strong cash flow growth will continue. Salesforce expects fiscal 2027 operating cash flow and free cash flow growth of approximately 4%-5%. This is considerably slower than the increase registered in the last reported quarter. Expanding Agentforce and Data 360 will require continued investment to support future growth.

Salesforce appears capable of maintaining substantial shareholder returns, although slower cash flow growth could limit the scope for significantly larger payouts in the near term.

How Do Rivals Fare Against Salesforce on Cash Returns?

Microsoft Corporation MSFT is a strong benchmark for Salesforce's cash-generation and shareholder-return strategy. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company generated $58 billion in operating cash flow.

During the first quarter, Microsoft returned $11.1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Its substantial cash generation gives it considerable flexibility to reward investors while funding growth.

Oracle Corporation ORCL offers a contrasting picture. The company generated a record operating cash flow of $23 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. However, aggressive capital investment to support cloud infrastructure growth and customer demand pushed free cash flow into negative territory at $5.4 billion.

title: ServiceNow Drops 29% in a Month: Should You Hold or Fold the Stock?

ServiceNow Drops 29% in a Month: Should You Hold or Fold the Stock?
Aniruddha Ganguly

ORCL

CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

ServiceNow NOW shares have dropped 29% in the past month, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's fall of 12.6%. The company's shares have also lagged peers, including Oracle ORCL, Salesforce CRM and Microsoft MSFT, shares of which have declined 14.1%, 8.7% and 28.5%, respectively, over the same time frame. NOW's underperformance can be attributed to investor concerns over slowing near-term backlog growth, modest guidance increases, acquisition-related risks and uncertainty over the monetization of artificial intelligence (AI). Let's delve deep to find out what investors should do with the NOW stock.

NOW Stock's Price Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

NOW Stock Suffers From Modest Expectations

ServiceNow's fourth-quarter 2026 current remaining performance obligations (cRPO) outlook has been disappointing. The company expects cRPO growth of 18.5% in constant currency (cc) compared with 21% in the third quarter of 2026. The projected slowdown has raised concerns about future subscription revenue growth. NOW attributed the deceleration to early renewals in the third quarter, a higher mix of on-premises public-sector contracts, deployment-related accounting adjustments and termination-for-convenience provisions that exclude certain backlog from cRPO.

ServiceNow raised its 2026 subscription revenue guidance by only $15 million at the midpoint, to $15.785 billion. This relatively small increase may have disappointed investors expecting a stronger outlook from the company's accelerating AI business. NOW explained that its decision to include deployment expertise with certain large customer agreements is shifting some revenues from subscriptions to professional services. This reduced subscription revenue growth by approximately 25 basis points (bps) in the third quarter and is expected to create a 50-bps headwind in the fourth quarter.

ServiceNow's expansion through acquisitions is another potential source of investor concern. The company's Armis acquisition is expected to contribute approximately 175 bps to fourth-quarter subscription revenue growth in cc but reduce non-GAAP operating margin by approximately 75 bps. NOW's growing exposure to cybersecurity also increases integration complexity as it combines acquired technologies with its broader AI platform.

NOW Faces Profitability and Debt Challenges

ServiceNow faces mounting profitability challenges due to higher infrastructure expenses and acquisition-related costs. In the third quarter of 2026, subscription cost of revenues increased 58% year over year to $1.05 billion, significantly outpacing subscription revenue growth of 21%. Consequently, GAAP subscription gross margin contracted to approximately 74% from 80% in the year-ago quarter. Higher third-party cloud expenses, employee costs and amortization of acquired intangible assets contributed to the deterioration. Sustained investment in AI infrastructure and cybersecurity offerings could continue to pressure profitability despite improving operating efficiencies.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NOW's 2026 earnings has declined by 2.7% to $3.95 per share over the past 30 days and indicates 12.5% growth from 2025's reported figure. The consensus mark for NOW's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings estimate is currently pegged at $1.08 per share, down 6.1% over the past 30 days and suggests 17.4% growth over the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Mercor raises $750m to expand AI evaluation tools for enterprises
AI data company Mercor lands $750m funding at $20bn valuation. · Verdict · Wanan Wanan/Shutterstock.com.
Anwesha Pattanaik

Trading disclosure

US-based Mercor has announced the completion of a $750m Series D funding round, bringing the AI data company's valuation to $20bn.

The new capital is expected to support the expansion of Mercor's evaluation and post-training services. These services aim to help organisations measure and standardise the performance and reliability of AI agents across a range of business functions.

Participants in the financing round include investment companies such as Benchmark, Fundomo, Felicis, and funds managed by affiliates of G Squared, Apollo, General Catalyst, and Glade Brook Capital.

The funding round also saw the participation of Nvidia, Sapphire Ventures, Salesforce, StepStone Group, XTX Ventures, and Zoom.

Mercor provides tools for companies to train and validate AI with human expertise, tailoring models to meet specific business needs.

Mercor co-founder and co-CEO Brendan Foody said: "Every job in the economy will need its own AI agents, and every company will need a way to train and evaluate them on its own work.

"We spent the last two years building that infrastructure with the frontier labs. Now we're bringing it to enterprises across the economy."

According to Mercor, the demand for domain-specific AI systems is increasing as model capabilities advance.

Mercor co-founder and co-CEO Adarsh Hiremath said: "Every company deploying AI needs to know whether it works, and the answer is different for each one. A model can score well on a public benchmark and still fail on the systems, policies, and edge cases that define how a specific business runs.

"We build custom benchmarks with each enterprise to measure models against its own standards, and that benchmark becomes the starting point for post-training."

Earlier this year, Mercor acquired Deeptune, a company known for reconstructing hundreds of enterprise applications into training environments over a two-year period.

This move is intended to enhance Mercor's ability to offer realistic environments where AI agents can be trained on complex professional tasks.

The company's efforts build on APEX, its public benchmark series designed to assess how AI performs in economically relevant scenarios.

The additional funding is set to further Mercor's research and investment in infrastructure dedicated to the evaluation and post-training of AI models.

"Mercor raises $750m to expand AI evaluation tools for enterprises" was originally created and published by Verdict, a GlobalData owned brand.

title: What Are ServiceNow Stock Bears Missing?
detail:
What Are ServiceNow Stock Bears Missing?
Trefis Team
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 3:13 PM MST 4 min read
NOW
^GSPC
CRM
TEAM
WDAY
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

One business stands out at ServiceNow (NOW): the AI products it sells to large enterprises, and bulls appear to be betting on exactly that. Bears have price on their side, with the stock down 40.2% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 returned 13.7%. To prove them wrong, ServiceNow has to sustain its rapid AI sales growth and improve its reported profit margin, which has fallen over the past year. So how fast are ServiceNow's AI sales growing?

ServiceNow Keeps Raising Its AI Sales Target

They are growing fast, according to management's own figures. On the October 28, 2026 call, management said the value of new yearly contracts for ServiceNow's AI products grew 65% in fiscal Q3 2026 from a year earlier. The company began the year with a $1 billion AI target for year-end and raised it to $1.5 billion in May. Management then raised the target again on the October call, pushing it to more than $1.7 billion.

Individual products are also growing quickly. EmployeeWorks, which handles employees' workplace service requests, reached $100 million in yearly contract value in less than three quarters. On November 4, 2026, ServiceNow said the NBA will deploy EmployeeWorks for its own employees.

Management expects AI to become a large part of the business. During its Financial Analyst Day in May, the company set a goal for AI to make up 30% of its yearly contract value by 2030, and management said on the October call that ServiceNow was on that path. On AI sales, the bulls have the evidence so far.

Is ServiceNow Turning Its AI Growth Into Profit?

Not on its reported figures yet, and that is where the bears have a point. ServiceNow's operating margin was 9.4% in fiscal Q3 2026, down from 16.8% a year earlier. Its gross margin fell to 70.5% from 77.3% over the same year. On management's own measure, its non-GAAP operating margin was 32.5% in fiscal Q3 2026, which differs from the reported margins above. That beat the company's own guidance by 150 basis points.

ServiceNow looks stronger on cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after capital spending, was $748 million in fiscal Q3 2026, up from $569 million a year earlier. So ServiceNow's free cash flow has grown along with its sales, while its reported margins have fallen even as its AI sales took off.

What Would Show ServiceNow's AI Sales Falling Short?

ServiceNow's AI sales would be falling short if the company's overall growth never picked up. It has not picked up yet, so that test is still open. Revenue grew 20.5% from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026, against 21.8% in fiscal Q3 2025. Management's AI growth figure is new contract value, not reported revenue, so it covers what customers have signed, not what has reached the income statement.
